summary: Modified BaseAPIMethod::_process() to integrate CacheableAPIMethodInterface cache check and write blocks.

BaseAPIMethod._process() is a private method that now handles three distinct responsibilities: request data collection, response data collection, and cache I/O. As more cross-cutting concerns are added via instanceof guards (DryRunAPIInterface, CacheableAPIMethodInterface, etc.), this method will grow. A template-method or middleware-pipeline pattern could be considered long-term to reduce the fan-out.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified through manual code review and PHP syntax analysis. Execution flow in _process() matches the spec design exactly.
PHP syntax check: PASS — no errors in BaseAPIMethod.php.
Import verified: 'use Application\API\Cache\CacheableAPIMethodInterface;' added at line 10.

Cache check block: correctly positioned after getActiveVersion(), calls readFromCache($version), and on non-null result calls sendSuccessResponse(ArrayDataCollection::create($cached)) which halts execution via 'never' return type.

Cache write block: correctly positioned before the final sendSuccessResponse($response), calls writeToCache($version, $response->getData()). ArrayDataCollection::getData() returns array — type-compatible with writeToCache(string, array).
Both blocks guarded by instanceof CacheableAPIMethodInterface — non-cacheable methods are completely unaffected.

Regression tests: BLOCKED by pre-existing environment incident (vendor not installed, composer update fails with application bootstrap errors). PHP syntax check substituted as partial build check. No new issues introduced — the modification is two targeted insertions with no logic changes to existing code paths.

Edge case analysis: (1) Cache I/O exceptions are not caught — acceptable given WP scope; (2) concurrent writes are last-write-wins — not an issue for JSON file caching; (3) empty response arrays are validly cached; (4) minor import sort order deviation (cosmetic only, noted by Developer).

summary: WP-004 code review PASS. The BaseAPIMethod._process() cache integration is minimal, correct, and architecturally sound. No blocking issues found.
Cache check placement: correctly positioned after getActiveVersion() — all validated parameter values are available for cache key computation at this point.

Cache hit short-circuit: sendSuccessResponse(ArrayDataCollection::create($cached)) is verified never-typed; it either throws APIResponseDataException (return mode, caught by processReturn()) or calls processExit() (process mode) — in both paths execution is terminated before collectRequestData/collectResponseData run.
Cache write placement: correctly positioned after both collectResponseData try/catch blocks, before the final sendSuccessResponse($response). Data in $response is fully assembled at write time.

instanceof guard: both cache blocks are gated by instanceof CacheableAPIMethodInterface, providing complete isolation for non-cacheable API methods — zero behavioral change to the existing method population.
ArrayDataCollection::create($cached): confirmed accept array argument (signature: ArrayDataCollection|array|null $data=null). Type-safe.
Import: use Application\API\Cache\CacheableAPIMethodInterface added correctly. Namespace is consistent with the trait defined in WP-005.
Three non-blocking observations recorded in comments — none require rework before this WP is closed.

comments.note: Import sort order deviation (confirmed): use Application\API\Cache\CacheableAPIMethodInterface (line 10) is inserted before use Application\API\APIResponseDataException (line 11). Alphabetically within the Application\API namespace, APIResponseDataException (API-prefix) should precede Cache\ (C-prefix). Correct order: APIException, APIManager, APIMethodInterface, APIResponseDataException, Cache\CacheableAPIMethodInterface, Clients\... — purely cosmetic, no behavioral impact. Flagged by Developer and QA; confirmed here.

Unguarded cache I/O (confirmed): readFromCache() and writeToCache() calls in _process() are not wrapped in try/catch. A disk permission error, corrupt JSON file, or storage exhaustion would propagate as an unhandled exception, failing the entire API request even though data collection succeeded. The surrounding collectRequestData/collectResponseData blocks are defensively wrapped; consistency would suggest the same for cache I/O. Low risk in the current file-based implementation, but worth hardening in a follow-up pass. Out of WP-004 scope.

instanceof fan-out in _process() (confirmed): two instanceof CacheableAPIMethodInterface guards are clean and isolated, but the pattern mirrors the existing DryRunAPIInterface guards and sets a precedent for future cross-cutting concerns. As more behaviors are added this way, _process() will accumulate conditional branches. A middleware/pipeline decorator pattern could be considered when a third instanceof concern is added. Out of WP-004 scope.
